abstract: The loss of proteostasis is one of the primary drivers of aging. Despite the important role of the molecular chaperone HSP90 in maintaining proteostasis, its systemic role in aging appears contradictory because its inhibitors can effectively extend lifespan across diverse species. This study showed that dietary HSP90 supplementation via Escherichia coli significantly extended lifespan and healthspan of Caenorhabditis elegans without fertility trade-offs. Exogenous HSP90 likely acts as an extracellular signaling ligand that engages downstream kinase networks to drive the activation of three major longevity-associated transcription factors: DAF-16, SKN-1, and HSF-1. In addition, we demonstrated the additive effect of combining dietary HSP90 supplementation with the senolytic HSP90 inhibitor tanespimycin, indicating that extracellular proteostatic signaling and the intracellular inhibition of HSP90 can work together to enhance longevity. Finally, we engineered an antibiotic-free E. coli Nissle 1917 probiotic that constitutively expresses HSP90, which successfully extended the lifespan of C. elegans.
